description:

const tabsetID = document.getElementById("GLM_RESULTS_TAB");

I have started working on this and solved a number of issues already:

- adding many `wait_ = FALSE` to my tests because the remote Shiny instance is not in test mode, hence not responding when output values don't change (see bottom section in https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest/articles/in-depth.html#setting-inputs-with-appsetinputs)

I am now seeing 404 errors at `$url/session/.../dataobj/shinytest?...`, probably due to https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b52b9e4520ad8d1e976299d5dec5e4ba3096bd04/R/shiny.R#L472-L474

Is there a way around that?
1. Can I run `shinytest` without the remote `dataobj/shinytest` (probably not)?
2. Can I activate test mode remotely (probably not)?
3. Can I safely activate test mode on our public Shiny instance, or is there any downside (probably yes if 2 is a no)

title: `devtools::test()` requires *installed* package
description:
As per current instructions:

https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest/blob/8715e57a149a8350ea30bec5d3f010343414044e/vignettes/package.Rmd#L109-L113

I think a successful `testthat::test_package()` requires the package in question to be installed (via, e.g. `remotes::install_local()`).

Otherwise, for example:

```
Error (test-shiny.R:5:3): hello_world_app() works
Error: Error starting application:
Loading required package: shiny
Error in library(wama) : there is no package called ‘wama’
Backtrace:
  1. shinytest::expect_pass(...) test-shiny.R:5:2

  3. base::lapply(...)
  4. shinytest:::FUN(X[[i]], ...)
  5. base::source(testname, local = env)
  7. [ base::eval(...) ] with 1 more call
  9. ShinyDriver$new("../../")
 10. shinytest:::initialize(...)
 11. shinytest:::sd_initialize(...)
 12. private$startShiny(...)
 13. shinytest:::sd_startShiny(...)
```

This is somewhat counter to the usual `testthat::test_*()` logic, many of which seem to be running (and are happy with) `devtools::load_all()` under the hood.

I'm guessing this is because shinytest spins up a new process or something, where it doesn't have the same environment available that other tests have, and thus lacks the objects resulting from `load_all()`.

title: Silently not loading JavaScript files
description:
I've noticed that `shinytest` sometimes (silently) does not load JavaScript files.  In order to pinpoint what might be going on, I've created a reprex here:  https://github.com/mdlama/reprex-shinytest-js-inclusion-bug.

In that reprex, I've taken the [Shiny custom input binding example](https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/custom-input-bindings.html) and added two lines to the [url-input-binding.js file](https://github.com/mdlama/reprex-shinytest-js-inclusion-bug/blob/main/www/url-input-binding.js): 

 1.  a `console.log` at the top of the JS file to alert that the file has been sourced, and 
 2.  the line `Math.max(...[0, 1, 2]);` in the `find` function for the input binding.  

This code uses the spread operator, which from what I can gather might be problematic for PhantomJS (see [this ticket](https://github.com/ariya/phantomjs/issues/15187)).

Based on [another shinytest ticket](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest/issues/317) pointing out that PhantomJS doesn't handle modern JavaScript, I'm inclined to believe this is a PhantomJS issue which will likely go away once headless Chrome is included as the default headless browser.

I wasn't sure if this ticket was needed but I had a heck of a time finding anything out there discussing this issue of silently not including JS files.  Plus, not 100% sure it is a PhantomJS issue.  Also not sure why no warning is given!

Thanks!

## Introduction
I am developing an app that uses modules and am wondering whether it is possible to use shinytest for that app. You can find the source code for the app [here](https://github.com/EarthSystemDiagnostics/cpt-picarr/). The app.R file is [here](https://github.com/EarthSystemDiagnostics/cpt-picarr/blob/master/R/app.R).

I would greatly appreciate you help on this. Thanks in advance!
Tom

Upon trying to record a test with `shinytest` I got the following error:
```R
Warning: Error in eval: object 'ShinyDriver' not found
  61: eval
  60: eval
  59: match.arg
  48: app$getDebugLog

   1: shinytest::recordTest
```

## Own research

Looking at the [docs](https://rstudio.github.io/shinytest/reference/ShinyDriver.html) for `ShinyDriver` I found the following piece of information:
> Currently it [ShinyDriver] supports apps that are defined in a single app.R file, or in a server.R and ui.R pair.

It is unclear whether or not this applies to our app. We use modules and helper files, however we also have a file `app.R` that brings all the application logic together.

Looking further I found [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest/issues/3) where someone is encountering issues when trying to use shinytest with modules.

I also found [this blog post](https://www.r-bloggers.com/shiny-modules/) that makes it seem like shinytest and modules can be used together. In the blog post they use a different directory structure (app.R in inst/app/; modules in R/). Maybe using the different directory structure can solve my issue.

title: Request: Option to ignore certain files when running snapshotCompare()
description:
I am using shinytest within an application that lets the user download a powerpoint slide deck (produced by [`officer`](https://davidgohel.github.io/officer/)).  Part of my tests involve making sure the download functionality of the slides is working.  I have the following line in my test script to trigger a download (`download_slides` is the `outputId` of the download button):

```r
app$snapshotDownload("download_slides", filename = "test_slide_download.pptx")
```

The test script runs successfully, but one quirk of these exported powerpoint files is the file sizes can differ from one test run to another even though the actual content inside them is the same (that's a separate issue).  When the test run is being compared to the expected results, differences are detected in the exported files (and not the JSON) as seen in this output:

```
tmp <- testApp(".", "test-app.R", compareImages = FALSE, interactive = FALSE)

  viewTestDiff(".", interactive = FALSE)
```

In any event, I don't want the `.pptx` files to be compared when running `snapshotCompare`, as I will flag key reactive objects that have the textual content of the slides using `shiny::exportTestValues` so they can be compared easily alongside the inputs and outputs. title: Request: future testing support for shiny.js-only apps
description:

The only communications are from the UI, via `Shiny.onInputChange()`, and from the server side using `session$sendCustomMessage()`. We have no "outputs", but we could use the shinytest "export" feature to test the state of the application in snapshots.

It would be nice to be able to interact with shiny test using `app$setInputs(...)`, but of course when I manually try to add some of those to a test script, I get `Unable to find input binding for element`. Is there a way to "prime" shinytest to set up bindings for specified named inputs when the test script starts, so that we could later use `app$setInputs(...)` to pump data into the backend?

title: Testing inputs - edge case
description:
Here is the problem. Imagine that we have the following app below:

```r
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("add", "Add table", icon = icon("th")),
  tags$div(id = "tables")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$add, {
    id <- paste0("slider-", input$add)
    insertUI("#tables", "beforeEnd", DT::dataTableOutput(id))
    output[[id]] <- DT::renderDataTable(head(mtcars, 3), server = FALSE)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

I wanted to interact with (and test) this app in a specific way: I wanted to create one table, highlight a few rows, then create a second table and make sure that the highlighted rows from the first table are still there. This is not possible right now.

The first problem I encountered was that if you select rows when you run `recordTest()`, shinytest gets confused and even though it records the test and produces a tests directory, these are only for first snapshots (before clicking any rows and losing the rest of the information). This is especially bad because while you test the app (including selecting rows), there’s no indication anything is going wrong.

However, as soon as you finish recording the test, you get an error:
```r
> recordTest(“apps/insertUI-test”)

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7005
Saved test code to /Users/barbaraborges/shinyTestResults/apps/insertUI-test/tests/mytests.R
Saving baseline...
Error in session_makeRequest(self, private, endpoint, data, params, headers) :
  Unable to find input binding for element with id DataTables_Table_0_length
```

You get the same error when you try to test it:

```r
> testApp(“apps/insertUI-test”)
====== Running mytests.R ======
  Error in session_makeRequest(self, private, endpoint, data, params, headers) :
  Unable to find input binding for element with id DataTables_Table_0_length
```

You can get around this by manually editing the test script and commenting out any line that sets one of the "meta" DT inputs. In this case, it was the setting of each datatable's length (`app$setInputs(DataTables_Table_0_length = "10")`) that was creating problems.

However, I still can't test what I originally set out to test, which was whether or not the rows of the first datatable remain highlighted when I add a second one...

title: Recorder should be aware of output events
description:
When in load test mode, the recorder should be aware of when an input event results in an output change. There are two reasons for this: recording timings between events, and knowing when to set a timeout.

There are two scenarios:
* User sets an input, then sets another input. No output changes between those two steps. In this scenario:
  * It shouldn't wait for values. (The timeout value is irrelevant because it's not waiting.) This makes sense for load testing, because load tests have a `Sys.sleep()` between each input event. However, for correctness testing, there isn't a Sys.sleep() between events -- does it make sense to not wait at all?
  * For load testing, it should record the time between the two input events, and add a `Sys.sleep()` for that amount of time.
* User sets an input, browser receives an output, and then user sets another input. In this scenario:
  * It should wait for values, using a timeout that's (maybe) 3x the actual time it took during recording. This could be used for both load testing and correctness testing.
  * For load testing, it should record the time between the output event and the second input event, and add a `Sys.sleep()` for that amount of time.

title: More complex updates
description:
The idea is the following: you can also specify the expected output of a widget. Sg. like

```
app$expect_update_to(xcol = "blah", clusters = 4, output = list(plot1 = corrent_plot))
```

This will basically perform the update sequence, and then wait until the output has the desired value, or a timeout kicks in.

The tricky thing is to guess when shiny is done. My initial idea:
1. listen to update events (`shiny::value`) for the output widget (`plot1` above) and then
2. wait until Shiny becomes idle. When it does, compare the output to the desired one. 
1. If they match, success.
2. If they don't wait a bit more (until the timeout?) and compare again.

title: Numeric input doesn't recover from receiving bad input
description:
Using this shiny app:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput('num', "num", "5")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe(cat(input$num))
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

If I set the value of `num` to a bad value (not a number), and then set it to a valid number, the input still returns an `NA` value.

```
shinyapp$new(path = ".")$find_widget("num")$set_value("bogus")$set_value("8")$get_value()
```

If you take a screenshot, you'll see that the actual text inside the input is "bogus8", which means that the second "set_value" didn't actually replace the previous value

It's very possible that other inputs have similar issues, this is the first input I tried breaking
